resources.string: Android did not report storage space.
Includes what Able can\'t measure yet
Documents and downloads include only files Android shows to Able.
See how much space apps use
Usage access lets Able read each app\'s size and cache from Android. Able does not read your app activity for this screen.
Media access lets Able add up the size of your media files.
Asks Android to delete cached files of all apps. Apps rebuild them when needed, so they may open a bit slower once.

Able asks Android (through Shizuku) to free as much cache as it can for every app. Your files, accounts and settings are not touched. Android decides what to delete, so the result can be small or zero. Able measures free space before and after and shows only what was actually freed. Nothing needs to be undone: apps recreate their cache.
Android deletes temporary files of all apps. Your data is kept. Apps may load a bit slower the first time.
0 bytes freed. Android had nothing more to clear.
Android accepted the request, but free space could not be measured.
Select apps to clear only their cache.

Deletes only the selected apps\' temporary files, like Android\'s own \"Clear cache\" button in App info. Data, logins and settings stay. Able re-reads each app\'s cache afterwards and reports the measured difference.
About %1$s of cache. Data, logins and settings are kept.
Apps cleared: %1$d of %2$d. Freed %3$s. Android rejected the others.
Android lets only system tools clear other apps\' caches. With Shizuku, Able can ask Android to do it. Without it, use Android\'s storage settings or each app\'s App info.

Regular apps cannot delete other apps\' caches. Shizuku runs Android\'s own package manager commands with shell rights, after you start it and allow Able. Without Shizuku, open Android storage settings or an app\'s App info and tap \"Clear cache\".
Clears only temporary files created by Able. Works without Shizuku.

Select files to review them. For media, Android shows its own confirmation before anything is deleted; for a folder, Able asks first. Deleted files cannot be recovered. Able checks afterwards which files are really gone.
